newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - August 3, 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - August 3, 1997.

text.p: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - 03 August 1997 This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- SMURFIT PLANS US SHAKE-UP

Irish paper and packaging group Jefferson Smurfit has been working on a major restructuring of its US associate Jefferson Smurfit Corporation. The review is expected to result in the sale or demerger of the group's forest and newspaper business. The other major investor in the JS Corporation, Morgan Stanley, has also signalled its intention to realise its 34 percent investment in the US concern.
-- EVANS AND MAIL LINK FOR RADIO BID

Presenter Chris Evans has joined forces with DMG Radio, the commercial company owned by the Daily Mail and General Trust, to bid for the NW England regional radio licence due to be awarded later this year. The alliance, if successful in its bid, will see Evans' Ginger Group controlling 40 percent of the station and DMG the remaining 60 percent. Other bidders expected to emerge for the franchise include Scottish Radio and Border TV.
-- BT INTERNET AND VIDEO DEAL

British Telecom is expected to announce an alliance with Japanese electronics giant Fujitsu and Alcatel of France which will revolutionise the British phone network. Under the terms of the deal, BT's partners will supply equipment to introduce Asynchronous Digital subscriber Loops (ADSL) which are capable of turning ordinary phone lines into high bandwidth carriers.
-- HORLICK POACHES AT MORGAN

Nicola Horlick the fund manager whose resignation from Morgan Grenfell caused such a stir has begun recruiting for her new operation. Analysts expected Horlick, who is now setting up her own team at Societe Generale, to take a number of key managers with her. Peter Seabrook, former UK chief investment officer at Robert Fleming, is set to join her but so far only Graham Wethered has moved over from her former team.
-- IVERSON CALLS IN US HELP

Anne Iverson, chief executive at Laura Ashley, has hired strategic consultants in an attempt to turn around the company's fortunes. The US Parthenon Group is set to concentrate on improving Laura ashley's supply chain.
SUNDAY TIMES
---- HIGH POUND THREATENS 400,000 JOBS

There are widespread fears that the sustained strength of the pound could result in a massive shedding of jobs. Industrialists and economists have warned that at least 400,000 manufacturing related jobs will be lost because of the currency's strength. The situation is expected to worsen this week as it is widely expected that the Bank of England will further increase interest rates to 7 percent. But chancellor Gordon Brown has indicated no lapse in his tough stance against inflation and has been given the recent backing of the prime minister.
-- M&S IN FOOD PUSH AGAINST SUPERMARKETS

Britain's most successful retailer, Marks & Spencer, is set to increase its range of food products in order to challenge the big supermarket chains. Food already plays a massive role in the company's strategy, accounting for sales of 2.7bn stg last year, but M&S now wants to be seen as a real alternative to the large retailer rather than a specialist supplier of premium products. The ambition will be aided by last month's purchase of 19 key stores in prime sites across the country from Littlewoods.
-- HOLLICK PLANS CABLE TV GIANT

United News and Media is considering a move into cable TV as part of its strategy to create a 1bn stg rival to Cable & Wireless Communications. Under the proposals, yet to be finalised, United would command a significant minority share in a cable company formed by the merger of Telewest and NTL.
-- CAMELOT WARNS LOTTERY WILL MISS 9BN STG TARGET

Camelot the National Lottery operator is expected to warn that it will fail to meet its target figure for good causes unless the government reviews the gaming laws. In the annual report, group chairman George Russell is expected to call for a "single and sensible policy" covering all gaming activity. The move follows the granting of gambling licences to organisations and activities which Camelot see as an infringement of the National Lottery franchise.
THE OBSERVER
--- BSKYB LOCKED IN EXECUTIVE NEGOTIATIONS

BSkyB is locked in strenuous negotiations with its deputy managing director David Chance. BSkyB shares have plunged since Chance and chief executive Sam Chisolm announced their intention to resign. Chance, an architect of the company's digital TV strategy stunned the City when he announced his departure. Analysts fear that like Chisolm, Chance was not content to occupy the executive's chair only until such a time when Murdoch's daughter Elisabeth took the reins.
-- NEW REPORT WILL SOFTEN CADBURY GUIDELINES

The committee on corporate governance, a team of 11 headed by ICI chairman Ronald Hampel, will call for key points of the Cadbury code to be watered down and the requirement that companies split the role of chairman and chief executive be eased. Hampel's preliminary report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to outrage shareholder groups who had hoped for a tightening of guidelines and could set the committee at odds with the new government who have vowed to end profligacy in the boardroom.
-- CARLSBERG AND BASS IN DISTRIBUTION TIE-UP TALKS

Despite being blocked in attempts at a full merger, Carlsberg Tetley and Bass are discussing the formation of a distribution tie up. Under the terms of the deal, Carlsberg's distribution arm would be taken over by Tradeteam, a Bass joint venture with transport group NFC. The move would threaten 1,300 jobs.
-- RANK LOOKS SET FOR 250M STG SHARE BUY-BACK

Bingo-to-casinos group Rank is expected to return cash to shareholders despite forecasts of disappointing pre-tax profits.The money for the buy-back will come from the 1bn stg sale of Rank's share in Rank Xerox.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- BLAIR SAYS GEORGE MUST STAY

Tony Blair has ended speculation that Eddie George will be replaced as governor of the bank of England when his term expires next June. Some analysts are seeing this rare intervention as a sign of growing tension between 10 and 11 Downing Street. There is also speculation that George will be re-appointed for a two-year term rather that the full five.
-- LEEDS UNITED TO KICK OFF PAY TV

Leeds United Football Club hopes to be the first team to show its matches on a pay-per-view basis after clinching a deal with Cable & Wireless and General Cable. Chris Akers, the chairman of Caspian Group, which owns Leeds, said that a media company hopes to take a minority share in a subscription channel that he will be launching at the end of the year. CWC and General Cable will distribute the channel. Speculation has mounted that Granada Group will be the football club's partner in the venture although neither Akers or Granada would confirm this.
-- BZW ADMITS 20M STG LOSS

Barclays is poised to reveal a "black hole" of around 20m stg in the operations of its investment subsidiary BZW. The shortfall is being chiefly attributed to long-term fixed income contracts with building societies, which are sold as fixed income bonds.
-- BUSINESS "SPIES" DEFECT FROM THE US
Two of the big six accountancy firms - Coopers & Lybrand and Deloitte and Touche - are moving into corporate investigation, once the preserve of companies like Kroll Associates and Control Risks.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- TUBE'S 1.8BN STG BID TO TAX MOTORISTS

Motorists may be forced to pay a series of special taxes in order to finance a 1.8bn shortfall in London Underground's finances. The money would be used to invest in the system's crumbling infrastructure.
-- STANDARD LIFE IN 400M SWITCH TO CASH

Mutual Insurer Standard Life is set to take a 400m stg gamble that the markets are heading for a sharp downturn. The stock market has soared 26 percent in the last 12 months and there is widespread speculation that a correction will occur. Sally Crombie, Standard Life's investment manager expects shares to fall up to 15 percent within three to six months and has been pulling in purchases for the last two months. Smaller operators Scottish Equitable and Scottish widows are also scaling back their exposure.
-- BRENT CLAIM FOR 110M STG

Brent Walker is set to renew its battle with Grand Metropolitan over 100m stg it claims that it is owed over the purchase of betting chain William Hill. Debt-ridden Brent walker bought William Hill from GramdMet in 1989 and was subsequently awarded 117.5m stg by a court arbitrator after claiming that GrandMet had overstated profits ahead of the deal. Brent Walker is now claiming additional costs and interest.
-- WH SMITH IS TARGET

Bath-based Johnson News has started moves to take control of WH Smith's wholesale network. WH Smith's wholesale business, which analysts predict to be worth 400m stg, has been the subject of bid rumours since the chief executive Bill Coburn left in June.
